messages:
ada: quick note — ran a small sensitivity scan for speculative decoding on the new 13B-quant build (int8 + per-channel). results are messy but interesting.

morgan: nice, what did you measure? throughput / quality?

ada: both. latency median dropped ~22% for greedy->speculative hybrid with k=5, but top-1 token agreement with float model is down ~3.7pp on wikitext snippets.

jen: 3.7pp seems high. what's the eval protocol?

ada: quick summary: 2k prompts sampled from onboard suite (mix of longform Q/A, code, doc summarization). compare float baseline (fp16) vs quant int8 with same architecture. run speculative sampler with early abort threshold=0.6 and rerank disabled. logged token-level agreement, perplexity, and a small human-fluency microeval (50 prompts).

sam: can you paste the run command/config?

ada: sure —

ada: ```
./run_spec_scan.sh --model ember-13b-qint8 --spec-k 5 --early-threshold 0.6 \
  --prompts-file eval/onboard_mix_2k.jsonl --out results/ember13b_qint8_spec_k5.json 
```

ada: and config snippet:```json
{"batch_size":8, "max_new_tokens":256, "stream":false, "speculative":{ "k":5, "early_threshold":0.6 }}
```

riaz: did you enable kv-cache warmup / prefix caching? that changes token agreement numbers a lot.

ada: yes — warm-prefix enabled, cache_warmup=64 tokens for longform. we additionally tried a cold-run set (no warmup) and agreement delta increased to ~6.1pp (worse).

morgan: any quality regressions in human microeval? examples?

ada: microeval (50 prompts) flagged 6 outputs as noticeably worse: repeated phrases, occasional factual drift at long horizons. two examples where speculative path chose short repetitive token chunks.

jen: did you try raising early_threshold to 0.8 to reduce regressions?

ada: tried 0.7 and 0.8 on a 200-prompt subset: 0.7 -> latency 14% drop, agreement -2.2pp; 0.8 -> latency 9% drop, agreement -0.9pp. tradeoff looks smooth.

sam: what's CPU/GPU perf? cost-wise is int8 + spec still net win vs fp16 baseline with no speculation?

ada: int8 alone gives ~1.6x token throughput vs fp16 on A100 (sustained), speculative k=5 adds another ~1.25x over int8 for our mix, so ~2x vs fp16. energy/cost estimates: rough 48% cost reduction.

riaz: are we seeing any bias/regression correlated with prompt types? e.g., code vs instruction?

ada: yes — more regressions on code-generation prompts (token overlap measure drops ~5.5pp) likely due to tokenization quirks and short deterministic sequences — speculative sampler sometimes guesses semantically correct but syntactically broken tokens.

morgan: do we have logs of token probabilities for disagreement cases? can we inspect where speculative candidate deviates in distribution?

ada: saved token logits for disagreement tokens in results/ember13b_qint8_spec_k5.jsonl.lz — includes top-10 probs for each step.

jen: can you run a quick rerank-on-disagreement ablation? if we rerank candidates against the full model when speculative path disagrees we might salvage quality while keeping some speedup.

ada: planned that — quick check on 200 prompts: rerank on mismatch reduces regressions to ~0.4pp but latency penalty is nontrivial (drops speedup from 1.25x to ~1.06x). might be ok as a fallback policy though.

sam: maybe make rerank conditional on length remaining >64 tokens so we avoid small snippets overhead.

ada: good call. will test conditional rerank.

ops-bot: CI test job #82431 finished: spec-scan nightly for ember-13b-qint8 (k=5) — 2k prompts — PASS (baseline metrics generated). :rocket:

riaz: any differences between shard replicas? could be quant nondeterminism.

ada: we observed tiny variability across runs (±0.2pp agreement) — likely RNG/quant rounding. retried with deterministic seeds and pinned CUDA math mode, variance shrank.

morgan: items to follow up: 1) run conditional rerank (len>64) on full 2k suite 2) vs fp16 baseline with k sweep (3,5,7) 3) collect more code-specific prompts and eval token-level diffs 4) decide default early_threshold per workload.

ada: I'll kick off the conditional rerank sweep now and post logs. ETA ~3h.

jen: thanks. quick note — add a small human-eval of 100 code prompts if possible (labelers prefer code samples).

ada: noted. adding to job.

sam: thx. also can we surface a dashboard card in console for token-agreement % by model+quant+spec config? would help teams pick safe defaults.

morgan: +1 to that. ops, can we get a quick spike?

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-2147 "speculative token-agreement dashboard spike" assigned to eng-platform.

ada: summary action — running conditional rerank sweep, will upload results to results/ember13b_qint8_rerank_sweep.jsonl.lz and ping here. feel free to DM for quick samples. :slightly_smiling_face:

morgan: perfect — ping when done and we'll pick safe defaults for dedicated vs hosted lanes.
